feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and overstuffed with overlapping skills sections, which reduces impact and scannability.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions at the same organization show growth, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms strengthen impact.  
- Strong positioning for modern digital roles: combines strategy, CMS/web execution, analytics, governance, and multimedia well.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily. Consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond responsibilities. Several bullets describe duties (“led,” “supported,” “advised”) without clear business/results impact.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; punctuation around lists is inconsistent (e.g., “workflows and systems” vs. serial commas); “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically inconsistent unless intentional branding. No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding leadership in digital transformation would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your senior value proposition: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a more concise framing like “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel communications, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, and cross-functional stakeholder coordination. Strong track record translating technical and policy issues into clear, accessible content that supports advocacy, engagement, and organizational goals.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel/multi-channel communications” and workflow/systems language are repeated in Core Competencies.
- “Advocacy messaging” and stakeholder coordination also appear elsewhere; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/technical strengths will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, CV-aligned language: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Workflow automation & systems design • Public-sector / advocacy communications • Stakeholder coordination • Multimedia & live event production
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; “Multi-channel communication” should be “Multi-channel communications.”
- Prioritize more senior, differentiating capabilities such as governance, modernization, optimization, and automation over broader wording like “web administration.”
- Consider reducing to 6–8 items for stronger scanability and less repetition.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Digital strategy,” “analytics,” “multimedia,” and “workflow/systems” are already covered in more detail in Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact outcomes and make the freelance/full-time engagement feel equivalent to a senior embedded leadership role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping duties into impact-led bullets, e.g.:
- “Built and optimized digital workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia communications.”
- “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Led AI-enabled search development, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, search accuracy gains, time saved, or engagement improvements.
- Replace “Deliver CMS development…” with stronger verbs like “Implemented,” “Modernized,” or “Resolved.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with NACo web governance/analytics language; keep this entry focused on new consulting impact, especially AI search and campaign platform work.
- “Microsite” and AI search details already appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles. Lead with the website modernization, analytics buildout, and studio launch as the clearest director-level wins.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen outcome language where possible: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia series.”
- Add measurable results if available for email/social/analytics/governance: growth %, time saved, reporting adoption, publishing consistency, campaign performance, or cost reduction.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; either quantify leadership-level growth/results or cut it.
- “Publishing standards/editorial coordination” also echoes earlier NACo roles; frame this here as enterprise governance or cross-department operating model.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to executional leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing for a national association audience.”
- Tighten bullets and lead with outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show ownership and impact: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” sound soft; use direct verbs to avoid underselling.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize leadership scope and strategic value rather than repeating generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive terms:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance  
- Editorial operations and content systems  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector and advocacy communications  
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “audience-focused content planning” for “content operations” or “governance” only if those are not already overused elsewhere.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise web and content strategy for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Keep wording parallel: all noun phrases, no mixed styles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “governance,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is close to “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies; use one version consistently.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and current execution strengths, not every individual technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-signal items here unless central to target roles; keep SharePoint/Power Pages only if the job requires Microsoft ecosystem experience.
- Remove “jQuery” from this topline section; it dates the profile and is better left in Technical + IT if needed.
- If you want more impact, tie to scale implicitly: “Enterprise CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” align better with recent NACo/freelance work than standalone platform names.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve detailed tools for the technical section.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also echo Core Competencies—avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a software inventory rather than a senior capability statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT,” so this section should emphasize decision-making, reporting value, and optimization outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization.”
- Use grouped, senior-level language: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace weaker terms like “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboards and decision support”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy and measurement • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design and executive dashboards • SEO, content performance and conversion analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave tool completeness to the technical section.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; consider folding into one sharper phrase.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented, emphasizing production leadership rather than listing tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Operations**
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets such as:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery  
- In-house studio buildout and operations  
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, swap one tool-level bullet for scope/impact language: **Recurring advocacy programming and executive/event video production**
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing broad categories (“video production”) with narrow equipment terms unless framed as workflows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; this version should go deeper or more operational.
- Tool names like Premiere Pro belong in Technical + IT, so don’t repeat them here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” It should emphasize platform depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than read like a duplicate software list.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add level/scope where possible, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content architecture)** rather than just naming tools.
- If space allows, rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise web modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it was only lightly used; it weakens the senior-enterprise positioning compared with the other platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one as a simple platform list and use the other for broader capabilities.
- Avoid repeating Drupal/WordPress/SharePoint in multiple sections without adding context or proficiency.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, and automation work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value for a senior profile.
- If accurate, replace one generic term with a stronger, outcome-linked capability: **custom front-end components**, **deployment automation**, or **serverless scripting**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this section more tool-specific.
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere, so GitHub Actions should stay framed as deployment/CI rather than broad automation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by strongest/most relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- Consider grouping to show function, not just apps: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If true, add light specificity elsewhere in the CV, not here, such as: “built cross-team workflow systems in Airtable/Power Automate” or “managed editorial planning in Jira/Asana”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools for the candidate’s communications leadership profile, but this line is too bare and misses the scale/enterprise context shown in recent roles. It would be stronger if framed around email operations and member engagement rather than just listing products.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and standardize: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to show enterprise use, e.g. **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation)** • **Higher Logic (member email/community communications)** • **Mailchimp**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, place it first to reflect recency and credibility.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets already covering email/newsletter leadership; keep this section tool-focused only, without repeating audience size or channel ownership.
- “Engagement” is broad; avoid implying CRM/community depth unless supported elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs or scale if you can add them.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Emphasize foundational impact: “Helped establish publishing workflows and day-to-day digital production processes that improved coordination across channels.”
- Make outputs specific: “Supported a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten management phrasing: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate” or “supervised daily work of a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this version focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the 2022–2024 role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around distinct contributions so it doesn’t overlap too much with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Lead with the standout achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Make the rest more specific and concise: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting county-focused programs and policy initiatives.”
- Combine digital/media support into one sharper phrase: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and organizational storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or outcomes: number of episodes, audiences served, program areas supported, or any adoption/engagement result.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.
- Avoid broad “supporting organizational programs and policy work” language if similar phrasing appears elsewhere; specify the type of projects or stakeholders.
